title: Pulse profile file
description: Named profiles of the engines Pulse reaches, and the default one. Where a file comes from decides what it may hold of credentials: a file others share (a repository's .pulse.json) names none, neither a secret nor the variable that holds one; the profiles of an MCP server name only variables that start with ENGINE_SECRET_; your own config file of the CLI may hold a secret itself. JSON Schema cannot tell which file this is, that a key appears twice, that defaultProfile names one of the profiles or that a URL is well-formed: the parser of @miragon/pulse-profile checks these and refuses the one profile they concern.

$schema.description: The URL or path of this schema, so that your editor checks the file.

defaultProfile.description: The profile a client uses when none is named. Blank means none; otherwise it names one of the profiles of this file. Without it, the only profile of a file is the default.

profiles.description: The profiles by name: letters, digits, ".", "_" and "-", starting with a letter or digit. The name is how you select a profile, and on an MCP server the engine id.

url.description: The REST API root, e.g. http://localhost:8080/engine-rest: an http or https URL without credentials, query or fragment.

cockpitUrl.description: The engine's web app, for links only, e.g. http://localhost:8080/camunda/app/cockpit/default/: an http or https URL without credentials, query or fragment.

engine.description: The name of a process engine (/engine/{name}); without it the default engine.

flavor.description: The product behind the URL; camunda7 when absent.

environment.description: The environment the engine belongs to (prod-eu, test): lower case letters, digits and "-". An MCP server groups its engines by it.

output.description: The CLI's output format; without it a table on a terminal, JSON otherwise.

headers.description: Extra request headers. A file others share stores no secret header: credentials, cookies and names containing token, secret, password or api-key.

not.description: Connection management headers the HTTP client sets itself.

^(?:[Aa][Uu][Tt][Hh][Oo][Rr][Ii][Zz][Aa].description: A secret header: only in your own config file of the CLI, never in a file others share.

readOnly.description: true refuses every write through this profile.

headerValue.description: An ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) value without control characters but tab.

auth.description: How a client authenticates. Without type a username selects Basic auth; OAuth and a stored token need their type. The secret comes from elsewhere: a variable the profile names, a login, or what each client keeps itself.

type.description: none, basic, bearer, oauth or passthrough (an MCP server forwards its caller's token). none switches the other keys off.

username.description: The Basic auth username: not blank, without ":" and control characters.

passwordEnv.description: The environment variable that holds the Basic auth password.

issuer.description: The OAuth issuer, discovered unless both endpoints are set.

authorizationEndpoint.description: The OAuth authorization endpoint; with type oauth only together with tokenEndpoint.

tokenEndpoint.description: The OAuth token endpoint; with type oauth only together with authorizationEndpoint.

clientSecretEnv.description: The environment variable that holds the OAuth client secret.

scopes.description: The OAuth scopes, each listed once; openid and offline_access when absent.

redirectPort.description: The port of the login callback; 0 for any free port.

tokenEnv.description: The environment variable that holds a bearer token obtained elsewhere.

variable.description: Only the name, never the value: letters, digits and "_", not starting with a digit. A file others share names none; an MCP server reads only variables that start with ENGINE_SECRET_.

secret.description: A secret itself: only in your own config file of the CLI. A file others share and the profiles of an MCP server refuse it; name the variable that holds it instead.

basicKeys.description: Basic auth keys: type basic, none or no type, and no key of OAuth or a stored token.

oauthKeys.description: OAuth keys: type oauth (or none, which switches them off), and no key of a stored token.

bearerKeys.description: A stored token: type bearer (or none, which switches it off).
